course_name_original: French B2 course - compulsory course of 135 hours for students of FIRST-CYCLE studies - semester 1/3
course_name_en: French B2 course - compulsory course of 135 hours for first-cycle students - semester 1/3
prerequisites: Knowledge of French at least at A-2 level.

learning_outcomes.text: Can write understandable informational and argumentative texts on general and industry-specific topics, conduct correspondence typical of a work environment, and independently use didactic materials.
Can clearly present conclusions and opinions on general, academic, and professional topics in written and oral form.

Understands longer, even complex written and oral statements, e.g., lectures and presentations, provided they relate to industry-specific issues and current affairs, and can interpret the acquired information.

Can use grammatical structures, phraseology, and vocabulary that allow understanding general texts describing contemporary economic and social phenomena, academic and industry-specific texts, and allow for fairly fluent and spontaneous communication in academic and professional environments.
Can prepare oral presentations on academic and industry-specific topics and participate fairly fluently and spontaneously in discussions, including in a professional environment.

syllabus_topics: GRAMMATICAL ISSUES - simple and complex relative pronouns - accentuating parts of a sentence (mise en relief) - comparisons - forming adverbs - future tenses (futur simple, futur proche, futur antérieur) - past tenses (passé composé, imparfait, plus-que parfait) - reported speech, sequence of tenses - agreement of past participle with subject or object - nominalization - passive voice - present participle (participe présent), gérondif - subjonctif - conditional mood, conditional sentences - pronouns y, en - personal pronouns, sentences with many pronouns - indefinite pronouns - past tense passé simple

THEMES AND VOCABULARY - Character description (external appearance, character traits, personality, requirements related to specific professions). - Consumer society (online shopping, contemporary consumer attitudes, auction sites, the phenomenon of sales, fair trade, household budget, student budget). - Education (teaching and learning methods, French education system, higher education in France, forms of classes, student life). - Elements of specialized and general technical language - Work (CV, job interview, labor market, job offers, employment conditions). Organization of work in an enterprise. - Mass media (press, radio, television) in France and Europe, reader/listener/viewer profile, the phenomenon of Francophonie). - Civil society (associations, humanitarian actions, social mobilization) - Culture and art (symbolic figures of French culture and art, painting, theater, cinema). - Ecology (threats, environmental protection, sustainable development, renewable energies). - Tourism, travel, multiculturalism.

LANGUAGE FUNCTIONS AND OTHER SKILLS - giving advice - expressing feelings - praising someone, making excuses - writing a letter/email requesting information, clarifying information - performing operations on French internet services - writing a complaint letter/email - negotiating prices - warning about danger - presenting professional qualifications - writing a CV, cover letter, commercial correspondence letter - filling out documents related to starting studies in France - filling out documents related to starting work - expressing consent - expressing opposition, forbidding something - speaking publicly - writing an informational text - writing a review - expressing cause and effect - questioning something, reporting unconfirmed events - expressing certainty and doubt - writing a petition, protest letter - expressing purpose - expressing duration - arguing and convincing - writing an internship report - talking about the future, presenting hypotheses - reporting events, presenting arguments - convincing, presenting one's arguments - planning a trip - understanding popular science statements and reports - understanding popular science articles - understanding texts related to the field of study - presenting a presentation related to the field of study.
assessment_rules: To pass, a positive grade must be obtained from all colloquia conducted during the semester. If a negative grade is received in the first attempt, the student can retake it. If a negative grade is obtained in the second attempt, the average of the two grades will be entered, and it cannot be less than 3.0 for a passed test. Unjustified absence from a test results in the loss of that attempt. Students are allowed two retake colloquia, with at least 2 days between them. The final grade is the arithmetic average of all grades obtained from passing individual semesters and the foreign language exam. Admission to the exam requires passing the compulsory language course semesters.
